title: Coping with fear of cancer recurrence (CARE-pilot): Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) versus cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) in cancer survivors and their spouses: a 2-arm randomized controlled feasibility trial
summary:
Fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) is one of the most significant psychological burdens faced by cancer survivors. FCR describes the fear, worry, or concern relating to the possibility that cancer will come back or progress, and is associated with reduced quality of life as well as other psychological symptoms. Approximately 60% of cancer survivors suffer from FCR, 20% of whom suffer from severe FCR. Relatives are also burdened by FCR, which in turn negatively affects the dyadic relationship as well as the survivors' quality of life. However, to date, there is a lack of evidence-based psycho-oncological couple interventions that focus on patients’/survivors’ and spouses’ FCR.
This bicentric study, coping with fear of cancer recurrence (CARE-pilot), addresses these research gaps and aims to test the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of a manualized ACT couple intervention for outpatient cancer survivors and their spouses. Sixty-four couples in which either survivor, spouse or both have elevated FCR will be randomized to either the ACT couple intervention (IG) or the traditional CBT couple intervention (active control group, CG). The primary endpoint of the feasibility study is the retention rate and achievement of recruitment targets. Using standardized measurements, changes in FCR, quality of life (primary endpoint of preliminary efficacy), and other psychosocial variables will be assessed at post-intervention and 3 months after the end of the intervention.
The feasibility study represents the first step in evaluating the feasibility and the practicality of the couple interventions. The CARE-Pilot study aims to evaluate the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of an ACT-based couple intervention in reducing FCR, compared to a CBT-based couple intervention, in couples navigating cancer survivorship.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- fluent in German
- able to take part in the 6-week intervention (one session per week)
- written informed consent
- living in a relationship or marriage (homosexual, heterosexual or diverse)

Inclusion criteria for patients/survivors:
- Cancer survivors (male/female/diverse) with any type of cancer 
- Having completed primary treatment (excluding endocrine therapy, which may still be ongoing)
- Less than five years since initial diagnosis
- FCR (FoP-Q-SF total score ≥ 34) or FCR of the partner (FoP-Q-SF/P total score ≥ 34)

Inclusion criteria for relatives:
- Partner (male/female/other) of a cancer survivor
- FCR (FoP-Q-SF/P total score ≥ 34) or FCR of the patient (FoP-Q-SF total score ≥ 34)
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for patients:
- Metastasis

Exclusion criteria for patients and relatives:
- Both the patient and their partner have low FCR  (FoP-Q-SF total score < 34 and FoP-Q-SF/P total score < 34)
-  Individuals who have participated in an ACT, CBT or mindfulness-based psychosocial intervention within the last two years
- Severe psychiatric disorders and suicidal ideation
